key_insight: LLM-guided feature discovery ranks protein–ligand poses more accurately than direct LLM reasoning, reaching up to 74% accuracy on Pyrite.
engineering_relevance: Automated pose ranking could help drug-discovery teams prioritize candidate binding geometries generated by cofolding models.
method: Build PyriteRep to encode molecular geometry, protein–ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores.
Compare direct pose reasoning with LLM-generated features used in logistic regression.
Apply Group Relative Policy Optimization to improve open-weight models.
evidence_signal: On a benchmark of 1,500 pose pairs, PyriteReasoner and PyriteFeaturizer achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, while tool-equipped expert chemists perform near chance.
watch_item: Benchmark ranking accuracy does not establish prospective drug-discovery value; generalization to new targets and pose-generation pipelines needs validation.
paper_title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
